Announcing the shortlist for the 2026 Prime Minister’s Literary Awards
Writing Australia has today revealed the shortlist for the 2026 Prime Minister’s Literary Awards, the richest literary prize in the nation.
Aug 10, 2026
The awards celebrate the exceptional talents of emerging and established Australian writers, illustrators, poets, and historians.
The Prime Minister’s Literary Awards acknowledge the contribution of Australian literature to the nation’s cultural and intellectual life.
Director of Writing Australia, Wenona Byrne , said:
“The 2026 shortlists reflect the extraordinary breadth, ambition and quality of writing being produced across Australia. These works invite us into new ideas, experiences and perspectives, while demonstrating the enduring power of literature to deepen our understanding of ourselves and one another.
“We congratulate all of this year’s shortlisted writers and illustrators, and thank the judges for the care, expertise and generosity they have brought to the selection process.”
Writing Australia is part of Creative Australia, the Australian government’s principal arts investment and advisory body. This marks the fourth year Creative Australia has delivered the awards, following the release of the Australian Government’s 2023 National Cultural Policy, Revive: a place for every story, a story for every place.
CEO Adrian Collette AM said:
“The Prime Minister’s Literary Awards recognise the vital contribution writers, illustrators and historians make to Australia’s cultural life. This year’s shortlisted works demonstrate the strength and diversity of Australian storytelling and its capacity to connect communities, challenge assumptions and enrich our national conversation.
“Creative Australia is proud to deliver the awards through Writing Australia and to celebrate the exceptional achievements of this year’s shortlisted creators.”
Creative Australia received a remarkable 673 entries across six literary categories: fiction, non-fiction, young adult literature, children’s literature, poetry, and Australian history.
Expert judging panels have carefully considered entries for the awards to select the final shortlists, including:
Children’s Literature
Bored – Felicita Sala
Little Bones – Sandy Bigna
Rain on the Rock – Valerie Brumby
Song of a Thousand Seas – Zana Fraillon
The Wondrous Tale of Lavender Wolfe – Karen Foxlee
Young Adult Literature
Blood Moon Bride – Demet Divaroren
Drift – Pip Harry
The Edge of Everything – Miranda Luby
The Foal in the Wire – Robbie Coburn
This Stays Between Us – Margot McGovern
Australian History
Fearless Beatrice Faust: Sex, Feminism and Body Politics – Judith Brett
First Tasmanians: A Deep History – Shayne Breen
Playtime: A History of Australian Childhood – Emily Gallagher
The Australian Wars – Rachel Perkins, Stephen Gapps, Mina Murray and Henry Reynolds
The Southern Frontier – Rohan Howitt
Poetry
Ghost of Myself – John Kinsella
How to Emerge – Jill Jones
KONTRA – Eunice Andrada
The Rot – Evelyn Araluen
Two Hundred Million Musketeers – Ender Başkan
Fiction
A Piece of Red Cloth – Leonie Norrington, Merrkiyawuy Ganambarr-Stubbs, Djawa Burarrwanga and Djawundil Maymuru
Arborescence – Rhett Davis
In the Name of the Trees – Merlinda Bobis
Out of the Woods – Gretchen Shirm
The Immigrants: Fabula Mirabilis, or A Wonderful Story – Moreno Giovannoni
Non-fiction
Blue Poles: Jackson Pollock, Gough Whitlam and the Painting that Changed a Nation – Tom McIlroy
Gather Up Your World in One Long Breath – S. Shakthidharan
Terraglossia – Dr Debra Dank
The Red House – Kate Wild
What Artists See – Quentin Sprague
The winners of the 2026 Prime Minister’s Literary Awards will be announced on Thursday 10 September 2026 at a prestigious ceremony held at the National Library of Australia in Canberra. The Awards offer writers access to Australia’s richest annual literary prizes, offering a total tax-free prize pool of $600,000. Winners receive $80,000 tax-free per category, and up to four shortlisted entries in each category receive $5,000 tax-free .
To read about the 2026 shortlists, including judging panel comments, please visit the Prime Minister’s Literary Awards 2026 page .
Download the media kit and social assets here .

More information:
The Prime Minister’s Literary Awards celebrate outstanding literary talent in Australia and the valuable contribution Australian literature and history makes to the nation's cultural and intellectual life. The 2026 Awards reflect an ongoing commitment to supporting and promoting Australian literature and recognising the important role books, stories and creative voices play in shaping Australia’s cultural identity.
Both the winners and the shortlisted authors will share in a tax-free prize pool of $600,000, the making it the richest literary prize in Australia. Each shortlisted entry will receive $5,000 with the winner of each category receiving $80,000.
For more information on the shortlists, including judging panel comments, please visit the Prime Minister’s Literary Awards 2026 page on the Creative Australia website. Join the conversation by using our hashtag #PMLitAwards.
